title: Rate it yourself: StillDrawn's human check

labels: No: it doesn't look hand-drawn — photographic, painted, or mechanically rendered
Yes: it could be a drawn panel
No: it stops looking hand-drawn — photographic, painted, or mechanically rendered
Yes: every frame could be a drawn panel
No: it became a different picture
Mostly not: much of it is different
Yes: nothing has been added, removed or replaced

questions.text: Does this original still image look like a hand-drawn black-and-white ink picture?
questions.direction: 5 = yes, completely · 1 = no, not at all
notes: Ink can stop looking hand-drawn **without** becoming photographic. Look for marks that no one drawing by hand would make: contours gone soft or blurred, edges that fade instead of ending crisply, lines that smear, warp or run together in ways a pen or brush would not, or shading that has turned into a smooth gradient instead of line or tone. **Clean, even linework, flat solid blacks and regular screentone are normal in manga and are not, by themselves, a departure.**

questions.text: Does this clip still look like a hand-drawn black-and-white ink picture, all the way through?
questions.direction: 5 = yes, completely · 1 = no, not at all
notes: Ink can stop looking hand-drawn **without** becoming photographic. Look for marks that no one drawing by hand would make: contours gone soft or blurred, edges that fade instead of ending crisply, lines that smear, warp or run together in ways a pen or brush would not, or shading that has turned into a smooth gradient instead of line or tone. **Clean, even linework, flat solid blacks and regular screentone are normal in manga and are not, by themselves, a departure.**
intro_notes: A slight overall shift in paper tone or brightness belongs here, mildly — a 4 rather than a 5. It is not a question-2 change.

questions.text: Apart from the movement itself, is this the same original image throughout?
questions.direction: 5 = yes, unchanged at every point · 1 = no, it became a different picture
notes: Anything **added, removed or replaced** counts as a change, even if the setting looks identical — a clip that adds a person to an empty landscape is not the same image.

**Action already in the drawing doesn't count.** If the original shows glass shattering, a figure mid-leap, or cloth blowing, then that action carrying on is the animation working — not a change. Count only things the original never contained: a new person, vehicle, object or lettering.

intro: First, the **still drawings** on their own. One question about each. This part takes about a minute.
Each screen shows an **original still image** (left) and a **5-second animated clip** made from it (right, plays on loop). You answer **two questions** about each clip.

The two are different questions and often have different answers. A clip can still look perfectly hand-drawn (a high answer to 1) while having turned into a completely different picture (a low answer to 2). How **much** a clip moves is not being asked about: a clip that barely moves but keeps everything intact is still a 5 on question 2.
Go with your eye. There are no right answers, and other people's answers will differ. You can change an answer with Back before finishing.
clips.watch_note: Watch the whole five seconds before answering. Things that appear briefly and then leave still count.

privacy: No names, accounts, cookies, IP addresses or browser details are stored. Opting in sends a random session id, your answers, their order and a rounded duration.
